blocks.passage:
Ethics is about doing the right thing, even when nobody is watching.

At work, there are many small ethical choices every day. Do you share a secret? Do you take the credit for someone else's idea? Do you tell a small lie to save time? Each small choice builds who you are as a professional.

A good rule is simple: if you would feel uncomfortable telling your family what you did at work, think twice. Honesty is not old-fashioned. It is the base of long-term trust.

audio.text:
I've just found a small mistake in a report — a number that's a little too high, which makes our results look better than they are. And here's the thing: nobody noticed. I could just leave it. But I'm going to correct it, and let me tell you why.

First, it's simply the right thing to do. The number is wrong. Correct results matter, even when they're less impressive.

Second, the family test. If my daughter asked me tonight, 'Did you fix the mistake you found today?' — I want to say yes. If I'd feel uncomfortable telling her, that tells me the answer.

Third, trust. If this wrong number went out and someone found it later, people would wonder what else we got wrong. One small lie can cost years of trust. One small honest correction builds it.

So I'll fix the number, and I'll quietly tell my manager: 'I found a small error and corrected it.' No drama. Just honesty.

Doing the right thing when nobody's watching — that's not old-fashioned. That's exactly what makes people trust you.
